transcript:
Header: 2026-06-21 14:00 PDT | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Daniel Kim (Redwood SE), Emma Clarke (Nova Health CTO), Ravi Patel (Nova Lead ML Eng), Karen Liu (Product)

[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm sofia from Redwood, and with me is daniel our solutions eng. how's everyone doing?
[00:06] Emma: good thanks, excited to see the hosted demo, we are evaluating options for chat assistant in care coordination, have some latency and PHI concerns so we want to understand hosted vs dedicated tradeoffs.
[00:14] Daniel: great — we'll start with a quick context ask then jump into a live demo of the hosted API streaming and call out parameters and retry best practices.
[00:22] Karen: quick note, legal might want SOC2/ISO docs, but product needs to see performance first.
[00:27] Sofia: totally, we'll cover security briefly and i'll share the security pack after. first, can i get a quick baseline of your traffic expectations?
[00:35] Ravi: sure, rough numbers — 50 RPS peak for top region, avg sequence length ~150 tokens, warm KV cache expected. latency target under 300ms p50 for short-turn prompts, p95 under 800ms ideally.
[00:48] Daniel: ok that's helpful. hosted is usually easiest to get started — predictable API, streaming for perceived latency, and we can suggest quantization/model variants if cost becomes issue. dedicated can give more consistent p95s but requires reserve.
[01:05] Emma: can you show streaming and how to implement retries? we've had trouble with duplicate responses when retrying.
[01:12] Daniel: absolutely. i'll share my screen — here's a simple curl + node sdk example in our docs. NOTE: transcription sometimes flips char cases in deck links, but link is in chat: https://redwood.example/deck
[01:28] Daniel: (screen) So for streaming, we use server-sent events chunking — client receives partial tokens as they're generated. here's node code: const stream = client.chat.stream({model:'rwd-large', messages, temperature:0.2}); stream.on('data', chunk => append(chunk.text)); stream.on('error', err => handle(err));
[01:47] Sofia: important to call out: streaming reduces time-to-first-token but doesn't reduce total compute cost; it's about perceived latency.
[01:54] Ravi: what about generating multiple candidates, i.e., n=3 — does streaming support that?
[02:00] Daniel: yes, you'll get streams for each candidate with separators; for most use cases we recommend single generation + rerank to save tokens. if you need n>1, watch token cost.
[02:14] Karen: parameters — can you quickly recap temperature, top_p, max_tokens, and stop sequences?
[02:20] Daniel: sure. temperature controls randomness (0-1), top_p is nucleus sampling. max_tokens caps output length. stop sequences tell the model where to stop; coupling with streaming you can stop local rendering when you detect stop token.
[02:37] Emma: any defaults you recommend for assistant style responses?
[02:40] Sofia: we usually demo temp 0.2, top_p 0.9, max_tokens 250 for assistant. adjust per prompt set.
[02:49] Ravi: retries — Operationally, we had duplicate responses because our client retried after a partial stream timeout. recommended pattern?
[02:56] Daniel: recommended approach: use request ids / idempotency keys and short-circuit on receiving partial stream token IDs. Redwood returns a request_id header; store that and dedupe on client. Also exponential backoff for 429s and idempotent retry for network errors only.
[03:18] Karen: do you have an SDK that handles streaming + dedupe?
[03:22] Daniel: yes, our JS and Python SDKs have streaming helpers and built-in request id propagation. i'll share sample repo.
[03:30] Emma: how do rate limits and quotas look for hosted? we're worried about burst traffic.
[03:36] Sofia: hosted has per-account quotas. for bursts we can enable burst capacity, or suggest routing policy to dedicated if sustained throughput. we'll send pricing tiers with quota numbers.
[03:47] Ravi: any auto-retry from your edge? or is it client-side only?
[03:51] Daniel: we do some short network retry at the edge for transient infra failures, but we recommend client-side backoff for request-level retries — avoids duplicating intents.
[04:01] (short pause, switching to live demo)
[04:15] Daniel: ok i'm calling the hosted API now, streaming a short assistant reply. you'll see partial tokens arrive. [04:22] (audible typing) [04:28] Daniel: (demo) partial: "Hi Emma — I can help summarize patient statuses..." then final payload.
[04:40] Emma: nice, that felt fast. what model is this behind the scenes?
[04:44] Daniel: in hosted we surface curated open models; this demo used rwd-large-1. we include perf profile and quantization variants — we can pin versions.
[04:55] Ravi: any mention of KV caching for multi-turn chats?
[04:59] Daniel: yes, Redwood automatically maintains KV cache for transformer states; for multi-turn you'll get cache hits which reduce compute for tokens referencing previous context.
[05:12] Emma: how do you handle PII/PHI in hosted mode? our compliance team will push back on sending PHI to hosted endpoints.
[05:20] Sofia: good question. hosted has options: customer-managed keys with KMS, data retention policies, and we offer private deployment or dedicated for strict PHI — we can show SOC2 and encryption docs. i'll include redwood security pack.
[05:36] Karen: do you have region controls for data residency? our EU patients data must stay in eu-central region.
[05:43] Sofia: yes, hosted supports region pinning for requests; we also have Private deployments for stricter residency and on-prem if needed.
[05:52] Ravi: on performance, do you provide per-token latency breakdowns in console?
[05:56] Sofia: Redwood Console includes token-level cost and latency breakdowns per model/route, plus tracing. we'll demo in follow-up.
[06:05] Emma: for PoC we'll want a short benchmark — can you run a test with our prompts?
[06:09] Daniel: yes, we'll run a benchmark during the PoC; please share representative prompts and expected concurrency.
[06:15] (discussion about pricing briefly)
[06:28] Sofia: pricing varies by model and deployment mode; hosted per-token pricing, dedicated reserved capacity. i'll send a hosted pricing sheet and trial key.
[06:36] Karen: what about integration time — how long to get something in prod?
[06:39] Sofia: for a simple chat assistant using hosted api, you can be integrated within days; PoC/benchmarks typically take 2-4 weeks depending on scope.
[06:48] Ravi: any SDK snippets for Ruby/Go or just JS/Python?
[06:52] Daniel: JS & Py first, community SDKs for Go/Ruby often exist; we can share contrib links.
[07:00] (moving to retry edge cases)
[07:10] Daniel: a common pattern: client sets timeout ~5-10s for time-to-first-token, but continue streaming; if timeout triggers before any token, retry once with exponential backoff. if mid-stream disconnect, resume is more complex — best to request short completions and re-ask with conversation state.
[07:35] Emma: are there webhook callbacks for async completions?
[07:39] Daniel: yes, we support async job API for long-running tasks with webhook notifications and polling.
[07:46] Karen: can Redwood handle function-calling / structured outputs? we need JSON responses for downstream processing.
[07:52] Daniel: yes, we have function/tool calling and structured output where model returns JSON; streaming can emit structured chunks and you can validate incrementally.
[08:05] (client question) Emma: are there any gotchas with stop sequences + streaming causing truncated outputs?
[08:11] Daniel: sometimes stop tokens appear mid-token in streaming; recommended to handle partial token buffers and check for stop tokens on finalization. SDKs have helpers.
[08:24] (roughly mid-call) Sofia: (recap) so action items: we'll send pricing and trial key, daniel to share streaming repo and retries doc, customer to send prompts and targets. anything to add?
[08:36] Ravi: also will need a security contact to do a quick SOC2/ISO review.
[08:41] Sofia: please send the email for security and legal and i'll loop our compliance lead.
[08:46] Karen: will do.
[09:00] (closing) Sofia: great — thanks all, we'll follow up with materials and set PoC kickoff next week. thanks for time!
[09:07] Emma: thanks everyone.

Note: transcription includes a few mis-hearings (e.g., Redwod used once), filler words, and occasional speaker attribution errors typical of automated transcripts. The demo covered streaming, params, retries, rate limits, region/residency, and PoC next steps.
